explanation: Barnacles are crustaceans. Their larvae swim freely, then glue themselves head-first to a surface and spend their lives kicking food into their mouths with feathery legs.

claims.text: Barnacles are crustaceans, like crabs and shrimps.
Barnacles are not molluscs like clams, mussels, snails and limpets, nor cnidarians like corals and anemones.
Barnacle larvae swim freely before cementing themselves to a surface head first.
Adult barnacles sweep food into their mouths with feathery legs called cirri.
